title: The Confusion

description.main: The second volume of the Baroque Cycle, made of two intercut novels, Bonanza and The Juncto, that carry its characters from Cairo to India, Japan, and the Americas and into European court and finance.
description.extended:
The Confusion is the second volume of the Baroque Cycle, built from two novels that alternate section by section: Bonanza and The Juncto.

It continues directly from Quicksilver with no time jump and moves across Europe, the Mediterranean, India, the Philippines, Japan, and Mexico. Bonanza follows Jack Shaftoe, who wakes from a long blackout as a former galley slave and joins fellow slaves in seizing a Spanish treasure ship that turns out to carry gold rather than silver. The Juncto follows Eliza, who loses her fortune to French demands and later works against the French invasion of England, and Bob Shaftoe, who serves in William III's Irish campaign. Its second half turns to Daniel Waterhouse, Newton and Leibniz, and to the founding of the Bank of England and the reform of the English currency. William Morrow published the 815-page hardcover in April 2004.

It is the middle of three volumes, between Quicksilver (2003) and The System of the World, and part of the backstory to Cryptonomicon (1999).

notes: First edition: William Morrow hardcover, April 2004, 815 pages. Volume Two of The Baroque Cycle, made of two books, Bonanza and The Juncto, printed in alternating sections.
